question.prompt:
There are \(20\) students participating in an after-school program offering classes in yoga, bridge, and painting. Each student must take at least one of these three classes, but may take two or all three.

There are \(10\) students taking yoga, \(13\) taking bridge, and \(9\) taking painting. There are \(9\) students taking at least two classes. How many students are taking all three classes?

solutions.title: Count class enrollments
solutions.explanation:
Adding the three class enrollments counts each student once for every class they take.

Let \(x,y,z\) be the numbers taking exactly one, exactly two, and exactly three classes, respectively. These groups include every student exactly once, so
\[
x+y+z=20.
\]
The students taking at least two classes give
\[
y+z=9.
\]
Meanwhile, the total number of class enrollments is
\[
10+13+9=32.
\]
A student in the first group contributes one enrollment, one in the second contributes two, and one in the third contributes three. Hence
\[
x+2y+3z=32.
\]
Subtracting the first two equations from this enrollment equation gives
\[
z=32-20-9=3.
\]
Therefore \(\boxed{3}\) students take all three classes, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
